name: µPC4570
tagline: NEC's 4.5 nV/√Hz, 15 MHz, 7 V/µs dual, pitched as a 4558 upgrade; Japanese modders hear tighter bass than NJM4580DD.

lineage.note: Original design, datasheet G10528; introduction year unknown. NEC Electronics until 31 Mar 2010.
From 1 Apr 2010; re-served NEC G10528EJ8V0DS00, then own R03DS0135 (2019, 2025). No second source.

part_numbers.note: DIP-8 (7.62 mm). Reportedly a maintenance product (保守品種); Renesas page live.
Renesas DIP-8 orderable; -A probably lead-free. Rochester Electronics via DigiKey Marketplace.
Sony part 8-759-111-44 in HCD-GRX80; suffix meaning unknown.
SOP-8 (5.72 mm); Renesas page live. Used in Yamaha AV-S70 (IC605).
Taped SOP-8 (-E1); -AP replaced -A after the 2024 back-end transfer.
TSSOP-8, −40 to 85 °C; covered by datasheet Rev. 2.00.
SIP-9; used in Tascam 238S. Not DIP-8 socket compatible.
LCSC/EasyEDA library name; genuine Renesas stock or clone unverified.

reputation.summary: A cult part among Japanese modders. NEC claims 3× lower noise and 7× the GBW and slew rate of the 4558; the C-Area wiki calls it 4558-derived, like the NJM4580. Versus NJM4580DD it has tighter bass, similar treble, maybe less resolution. Common in Japanese CD players, AV receivers and Tascam multitracks. No independent measurements found.
typical_uses: CD player output and filter stages
AV receivers and mini-systems (Yamaha AV-S70, Sony HCD-GRX80)
op-amp rolling as an NJM4580 alternative
caveats: DIP-8 µPC4570C is reportedly a maintenance product; aftermarket supply via Rochester Electronics.
Needs about ±4 V minimum; unsuited to low-voltage single-rail designs.
SIP-9 (HA) and SOP-8 (G2) versions do not fit DIP-8 sockets.
Sound claims are Japanese-community folklore; no independent measurements.
Tascam 424 MKI sound partly credited to its UPC4570 + NJM4565 (JHS 424 Gain Stage).

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit reports. DIP µPC4570C sells via surplus and hobby channels (Suzusho, AliExpress kits); Rochester Electronics is an authorised aftermarket source. Remarked vintage Japanese op-amps are a general risk. LCSC 'NEC4570G2' origin unverified; top-mark formats not seen.

silicon_changes.identification: Orderable suffix '-AP' (Cu wire) or '-AX' (Au wire, high-quality) replaces '-A' on SOP-8 (G2), e.g. UPC4570G2-E1-A → UPC4570G2-E1-AP. Top-marking rule unknown.
silicon_changes.summary: Renesas added (RL-BB-23-0058, June 2023; samples 25 Aug 2023), then transferred (RL-BB-24-0007, 19 Jan 2024, effective 13 May 2024) SOP back-end to UTAC Thai (UTL). Cu wire for -AP, Au for -AX. EOL260002 (Feb 2026) ends select old codes. Die unchanged; DIP, TSSOP not covered.

spec_deltas.after: different plating and wire specification. Exact materials were not captured. Cu wire on standard-quality -AP; Au wire on high-quality -AX codes.
minor dimensional differences; same recommended land pattern

silicon_changes.audio_impact: None expected: same die; plating or bond-wire changes have no documented electrical effect.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: same die and footprint; update BOMs for -AP and check outline for tight fits.
silicon_changes.verification: PCN text confirms UTL site, -AP/-AX mapping and dates; uPC4570 rows in EOL260002 not seen.

silicon_changes.identification: Datasheet number R03DS0135EJ (Rev. 1.00 / Rev. 2.00) versus NEC-era G10528EJ8V0DS00.
silicon_changes.summary: Renesas replaced the NEC datasheet with R03DS0135EJ: Rev. 1.00 (17 Jan 2019, 9 pages), Rev. 2.00 (27 Feb 2025, 11 pages), covering G2 (SOP-8) and GR-9LG (TSSOP-8). UPC258/UPC4558 also went to Rev. 2.00 that day. No changed limits found.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Unknown; no silicon change documented and datasheet deltas not known.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: same die as documented; check Rev. 2.00 limits before relying on NEC-era values.
silicon_changes.verification: Both revisions confirmed to exist; no revision notes or changed limits seen, so not confirmed as a respec.

open_questions: What else changed in R03DS0135 Rev. 2.00? It lists only G2 and GR-9LG; are C and HA discontinued?
Was the 2019 renumbering editorial, or tied to a fab or process change?
When were NEC editions 7V0 and 8V0 printed, and which mirror holds which edition?
Which uPC4570 codes are in EOL260002 (LTB 31 Mar 2026)? Confirm ±4 to ±16 V and the -1 suffix.
Datasheet i_n, THD, Iq, output current, Vos, abs. max? Is unity-gain frequency near the macromodel's 7 MHz?
